steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Add an import statement at the top of the file to import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the ES6 import syntax to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Component will be created in the next steps
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports to use React and the useState hook.
successCriteria: The import statement must correctly import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Remember to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create ThemeContext with createContext
steps.instruction: Create a React context for theme management by calling React.createContext. Name it ThemeContext and provide a default value of 'light'.
steps.hint: Use React.createContext to create a context object. Store it in a variable named ThemeContext and export it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of creating a context with a default value
const UserContext = React.createContext<string>('guest');
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a ThemeContext variable created using React.createContext with a default value of 'light'.
successCriteria: The code must include a ThemeContext variable created with React.createContext and a default value of 'light'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ThemeContext with a default value. This context will be used to share theme data throughout your component library.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using React.createContext with a default value of 'light' and naming it ThemeContext.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating just the ThemeContext. Use React.createContext('light') and assign it to a variable named ThemeContext.

steps.title: Define ThemeProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemeProvider that accepts children as props. The component should return the children wrapped in a ThemeContext.Provider element.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes children as a prop and returns children wrapped in ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeProvider component is defined that will wrap the app and provide theme context.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the ThemeProvider component that will wrap your app and provide the theme context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your ThemeProvider component accepts children as a prop and returns them wrapped in ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeProvider component needs to be defined with children as a prop and return them wrapped in ThemeContext.Provider.

steps.title: Initialize theme state in ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'theme' with an initial value of 'light'.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to specify the type for the state variable (string).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with useState
const [theme, setTheme] = useState<string>('light');
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component should have a state variable 'theme' initialized to 'light' using useState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the theme state with useState. This will allow the ThemeProvider to track and update the current theme.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check if you've: 1) Used useState, 2) Named the state variable 'theme', 3) Set initial value to 'light', 4) Specified the type as string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the ThemeProvider component, use useState to create a state variable called 'theme' with initial value 'light' and type string.

steps.title: Create toggleTheme handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, create a function named toggleTheme that toggles the theme state between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.hint: The toggleTheme function should call setTheme with the opposite theme value. You can use a ternary operator or an if statement to determine the new theme.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleTheme function is defined that switches the theme between 'light' and 'dark' when called.
successCriteria: Function uses setTheme to update state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggleTheme handler function that switches between light and dark themes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggleTheme function correctly toggles between 'light' and 'dark' themes. Check that you're using setTheme to update the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme function isn't quite right. Remember to create a function that toggles the theme state between 'light' and 'dark' using setTheme.

steps.title: Provide context value from ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Update the ThemeContext.Provider's value prop to pass both the current theme state and the toggleTheme handler function as an object.
steps.hint: The value prop should be an object with theme and toggleTheme properties. You'll need to modify the existing value prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeContext.Provider now provides both the current theme value and a function to toggle it to all child components.
successCriteria: The ThemeContext.Provider's value prop should be an object containing both 'theme' and 'toggleTheme' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully updated the context provider to pass both the theme state and the toggle function. This allows any child component to access both the current theme and a way to change it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the context value needs to include both properties. Make sure you're passing an object with 'theme' and 'toggleTheme' as properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The context provider value should be updated to pass both the theme state and toggleTheme function. Check that you're passing an object with both properties.

steps.title: Create useTheme custom hook
steps.instruction: Define a custom hook named useTheme that uses useContext to access ThemeContext and throws an error if used outside the ThemeProvider.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls useContext(ThemeContext). Check if the context value is undefined (or not an object with theme/toggleTheme) and throw an error. Return the context value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook that safely consumes the theme context, providing error handling for misuse outside the provider.
successCriteria: Check if context is undefined or not the expected shape
Throw an error if context is invalid
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a custom hook that safely accesses the theme context with proper error handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your useTheme hook calls useContext(ThemeContext), checks if the context is valid, throws an error when it's not, and returns the context value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useTheme hook should be a function that uses useContext to access ThemeContext and throws an error if used outside the provider. Try creating a function that follows this pattern.

steps.title: Create ThemedButton component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemedButton that returns a button element. Define a TypeScript interface for its props (if needed) and make sure the component returns JSX.
steps.hint: Start by writing a function or arrow function called ThemedButton. Since this button will use theme context later, you don't need props yet - just return a basic button.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemedButton component is created that can be used to render a button element.
successCriteria: Component is a valid React functional component
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ThemedButton component. This gives us a foundation to add theme styling in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a component named ThemedButton that returns a button element. Check that your component returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemedButton component wasn't created correctly. You need to define a functional component named ThemedButton that returns a button element.

steps.title: Consume theme context in ThemedButton
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemedButton component, call the useTheme hook to get the current theme and toggleTheme function.
steps.hint: Use destructuring to get both values from the hook call: const { theme, toggleTheme } = useTheme();
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemedButton component now has access to the theme context values through the useTheme hook.
successCriteria: The useTheme hook is called inside ThemedButton
The hook's return values are destructured into theme and toggleTheme variables
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully consumed the theme context in your ThemedButton component using the useTheme hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the useTheme hook and destructuring both theme and toggleTheme from it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemedButton component doesn't seem to be consuming the theme context. Remember to call the useTheme hook inside the component.

steps.title: Apply theme-based styles to ThemedButton
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemedButton component, add conditional styling to the button element based on the current theme value. Use inline styles with different background and text colors for 'light' and 'dark' themes.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator to conditionally apply different style objects based on the theme value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemedButton component will have different visual styles for light and dark themes when rendered.
successCriteria: The button element should have a style attribute with conditional styling based on the theme value. The styling should include at least background color and text color properties that differ between light and dark themes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional styling to the ThemedButton component. The button will now visually change based on the current theme.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the styling might not be fully conditional or complete. Make sure you're applying different style objects for 'light' and 'dark' themes with distinct background and text colors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button styling doesn't appear to be properly conditional based on the theme. Remember to create different style objects for 'light' and 'dark' themes and apply them to the button's style attribute.

steps.title: Wire onClick to toggleTheme in ThemedButton
steps.instruction: In the ThemedButton component, add an onClick handler to the button element that calls the toggleTheme function obtained from the useTheme hook.
steps.hint: The button element already exists. Add the onClick prop and call toggleTheme() inside it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of wiring a button click to a handler
<button onClick={() => handleClick()}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have an onClick handler that triggers the theme toggle when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element has an onClick prop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the button's click event to toggle the theme.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the button's onClick prop is set to call toggleTheme().
steps.feedbackWrong: The button still needs an onClick handler that calls toggleTheme().

steps.title: Create main App component with ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that wraps its content with the ThemeProvider component and includes the ThemedButton component inside it.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns JSX with ThemeProvider as the wrapper and ThemedButton as a child.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is created and properly wraps ThemedButton with ThemeProvider.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component that wraps the themed button with the ThemeProvider. This completes the theming setup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your App component includes both ThemeProvider wrapping the content and ThemedButton inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component needs to be defined with ThemeProvider wrapping ThemedButton. Check that you're using the correct component names and JSX structure.
